ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in square $ABCD$, $AB=9$, point $E$ is on side $CD$, and $DE=2CE$. Point $P$ is a moving point on diagonal $AC$. What is the minimum value of $PE+PD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw BP and BE,\\
since quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
thus AB=AD, and $\angle$BAP=$\angle$DAP.\\
since AP=AP,\\
thus $\triangle$ABP$\cong$$\triangle$ADP,\\
thus BP=DP,\\
thus PE+PD=PE+PB$\geq$BE,\\
meaning the minimum value of PE+PD is the length of BE,\\
since AB=9, and DE=2CE,\\
thus CE=$\frac{1}{3}CD$=$\frac{1}{3}\times 9$=3,\\
thus BE=$\sqrt{BC^{2}+CE^{2}}$=$\sqrt{9^{2}+3^{2}}$=$3\sqrt{10}$,\\
thus the minimum value of PE+PD is \boxed{3\sqrt{10}}.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In square $ABCD$, $AB=9$, point $E$ is on side $CD$, and $DE=2CE$. Point $P$ is a moving point on diagonal $AC$. What is the minimum value of $PE+PD$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Draw $BP$ and $BE$. Since $ABCD$ is a square, $AB=AD$ and $\angle BAP=\angle DAP$. Since $AP=AP$, $\triangle ABP\cong\triangle ADP$, so $BP=DP$. Thus $PE+PD=PE+PB\ge BE$, meaning the minimum value of $PE+PD$ is $BE$. Since $AB=9$ and $DE=2CE$, we have $CE=\frac{1}{3}CD=\frac{1}{3}\times 9=3$. Therefore $BE=\sqrt{BC^2+CE^2}=\sqrt{9^2+3^2}=3\sqrt{10}$. Thus the minimum value of $PE+PD$ is \boxed{3\sqrt{10}}.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a square ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; diagonal AC connects from A to C, point P is located on diagonal AC; point E is located on the right side CD, and the line segments from P to D and from P to E are drawn. Reasoning: Because AC is an axis of symmetry of this square, under reflection about AC, B and D are interchanged, and P is on AC, so for any such P there is PD=PB. Therefore PE+PD=PE+PB. By the triangle inequality, PE+PB≥BE; equality is attained when B, P, E are collinear and P is on BE. Check attainability with coordinates: Let B=(0,0), C=(9,0), D=(9,9), A=(0,9). Since DE=2CE and CD=9, CE=3, so E=(9,3). The line BE is y=x/3, and diagonal AC is y=9-x; their intersection is (27/4,9/4), inside the square and on AC, so equality can be attained. Finally compute BE: In right triangle BCE, BC=9, CE=3, so BE=sqrt(9^2+3^2)=sqrt(90)=3sqrt(10).
